mechanism: Instead of discrete hidden layers, NeuralODE parameterizes the derivative of the hidden state with a 2-layer ReLU MLP and integrates it with a Dormand–Prince (Dopri5) black-box ODE solver; adjoint sensitivity backprops through the solver. Per-feature weight matrices process 3-D tensors (embedding dim × variables × sequence length) so each market feature has its own continuous dynamics.
data_needed: Bar embedding sequence after Embedding+Conv+PE+CCMR; dimension/variables/length for CNeuronNODEOCL; OpenCL Dopri5 k1..k6 buffers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train first 7 months 2023 (~500 trajectories); test August 2023
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a continuous-time latent trajectory sensor: market state evolves as an ODE rather than discrete bar steps, so regime evolution rate and solver-adaptive step count become sensing signals.
quote: Instead of specifying a discrete sequence of hidden layers, they parameterize the derivative of the hidden state using a neural network. The results of the model are calculated using a "black box", that is, the Differential Equation Solver. These continuous-depth models use a constant amount of memory and adapt their estimation strategy to each input signal.

idea_name: Continuous Attention with Q/K time derivatives
mechanism: Conformer Continuous Attention attends across the same variable in different environment states (not within one state). Analytic dQ/dt and dK/dt are estimated from adjacent bar embeddings with unit time step (timeframe neglected), then scores use exp((Q·dK/dt + K·dQ/dt)/√d). Three NeuralODE layers follow attention; encoder embeds candle (4), RSI, CCI, ATR, MACD(2) separately.
data_needed: Per-variable embeddings over GPTBars; TimeDerivative + FeedForwardContAtt OpenCL kernels; RSI/CCI/ATR/MACD + OHLC features
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train first 7 months 2023; test August 2023
why_new_for_mis: Turns bar-to-bar change of Query/Key into an explicit continuous-change sensor—MIS can read how each indicator channel’s attention geometry is evolving, not only static cross-bar similarity.
quote: To compute Continuous Attention, the authors of the method propose to compute the derivatives of similarity for the same variables in each data sample. ... Instead of making forecasts predictions only for a certain time stamp, Conformer learns the transitional changes from one time step to another, which is important for capturing unprecedented changes in the weather.

idea_name: RevIN reversible instance normalization against distribution shift
mechanism: RevIN instance-normalizes each input series by its own mean/variance (optionally affine), runs the forecaster on stationaryized data, then denormalizes outputs with the same statistics via CNeuronRevINDenormOCL sharing BatchOptions with the upstream batch-norm layer—restoring non-stationary level/scale at forecast boundaries.
data_needed: Raw HistoryBars×BarDescr multimodal bars; batch-norm layer id for denorm; NForecast=6 targets
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train full year 2023 (Real-ORL + Research); test January 2024
why_new_for_mis: Makes distribution shift itself a first-class sensing object: MIS can monitor RevIN instance mean/variance as online regime level/volatility stats and use denorm residual as shift-detection.
quote: RevIN is a flexible, trainable layer that can be applied to any arbitrarily chosen layers, effectively suppressing non-stationary information (mean and variance of an instance) in one layer and restoring it in another layer of nearly symmetric position, such as input and output layers.

idea_name: Client cross-variable attention plus linear trend module
mechanism: Client transposes HistoryBars×BarDescr so sequence=variables and window=history; Transformer encoder does Self-Attention across variables (no embedding/positional encoding); parallel channel-wise MLP linear module extracts trends; forecasts are weighted-sum of linear and attention heads then RevIN-denormed. Masking tests showed temporal Cross-Attention often ignores history—variable attention preferred.
data_needed: HistoryBars=120 (≈1 week H1), BarDescr channels; mlp[]={1024,1024,1024,NForecast}; transpose+RevIN around CNeuronClientOCL
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test January 2024 (implementation failed to profit)
why_new_for_mis: Reframes MIS sensing from time-step attention to cross-variable dependence (price vs RSI/ATR/MACD co-movement) plus an explicit linear trend sensor—useful when temporal attention is noise-blind.
quote: The main idea of Client is move from attention over time to analyzing dependencies between variables and integrating a linear module into the model to better exploit variable dependencies and trend information, respectively.

idea_name: U-shaped multi-scale patch pyramid with HF skip paths
mechanism: U-shaped Transformer recursively merges patches via stride-2 conv (doubling channels) down the encoder and splits via transposed conv up the decoder; skip-connections inject high-frequency detail from matching encoder shapes; learnable PE from input-conditioned FC; pretrain by recovering Dropout-masked (p=0.4) inputs plus NForecast ahead.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr; nested CNeuronUShapeAttention blocks; Dropout mask; RevIN denorm of reconstruction+forecast
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a multi-scale HF/LF market sensor: coarse scales capture structure while skips preserve tick-level high-frequency context MIS often loses in deep stacks.
quote: During the input data encoding process, as the model moves down, high-frequency features are continuously filtered out while common features are extracted. During the decoding process, the general features are continuously reconstructed with the detailed information from the skip-connection, which ultimately results in a temporal representation of the series combining both high-frequency and low-frequency features.

mechanism: Multivariate series split into univariate channels; each channel is patched (non-overlap window=step=3) via CNeuronPatching embedding, then analyzed by channel-independent Conformer stacks sharing weights across channels—no cross-channel mixing inside Transformer. Learnable PE at raw input; 40% Dropout masking; RevIN denorm of reconstruct+forecast.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr transposed per channel; patch window/step; 10× Conformer with layers=BarDescr
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; indicators default params; test January 2024
why_new_for_mis: Treats each indicator/price channel as an independent semantic patch stream—MIS can sense local subseries patterns per channel without cross-channel contamination.
quote: PatchTST, in contrast, improves locality and captures complex semantic information that is not available at the point level by aggregating time steps into subseries-level patches. ... channel independence means that each input token contains information from only one channel.

idea_name: TiDE MLP encoder with timestamp covariates and global residual
mechanism: TiDE is channel-independent MLP: feature-project 4 timestamp harmonics (year/month/week/day) onto history and forecast horizons; dense residual-conv encoder/decoder stack; temporal decoder mixes decoded states with future covariates; global residual linearly maps past→horizon so pure linear AR is always a subclass; SumAndNormilize merges streams.
data_needed: Transposed BarDescr×HistoryBars; 4-D bTime harmonics; encoder_decoder[] hidden sizes; NForecast horizon
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a lightweight covariate-aware sequence sensor where calendar phase is explicitly projected into forecasts and a linear residual path senses pure trend separately from nonlinear MLP path.
quote: The Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE) model uses MLP to encode the past time series together with covariates and to decode the forecast time series together with future covariates. ... This ensures that a purely linear model is always a subclass of the TiDE model.

idea_name: FEDformer wavelet frequency attention and MOE trend decomposition
mechanism: Implementation uses Legendre-wavelet DWT (9 fixed polynomials) as Self-Attention substitute (CNeuronFEDW): wavelets→norm→SoftMax probabilistic spectrum→reconstruct→FF residual. Stacked FED-w layers then TiDE; MOEDecomp idea (mixture of average filters) motivates seasonal/trend split. Random frequency subset keeps complexity linear.
data_needed: Transposed univariate channels HistoryBars; CNeuronLegendreWavelets fixed basis; 10× FED-w + TiDE + RevIN
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test January 2023 (article text)
why_new_for_mis: Moves MIS sensing into joint time–frequency via wavelets and seasonal/trend experts—spectrum SoftMax weights are directly readable as regime/frequency-structure sensors.
quote: Instead of applying the Transformer to the time measurement of the sequence, we can analyze its frequency features. This helps the Transformer better capture the global properties of time series. ... a randomly selected subset of frequency components, including both low and high ones, provides a better representation of the time series.

idea_name: FITS FFT frequency interpolation with complex mixing
mechanism: FITS: RevIN-style norm → per-channel FFT → Dropout random frequency masking (stand-in for LPF/random harmonics) → separate real/imag conv MLPs → ComplexLayer combine → iFFT → crop to NForecast. Complex multiply encodes amplitude scale and phase shift jointly; ~84× smaller than FEDformer in author’s comparison.
data_needed: BarDescr univariate channels length HistoryBars; FFT padded to power-of-2; dropout rate; NForecast out window
why_new_for_mis: Ultra-light frequency-domain continuation sensor: MIS can track interpolated spectrum phase/amplitude as compact global-pattern features and Dropout-kept harmonics as sparse frequency fingerprints.
quote: FITS uses frequency domain interpolation to expand the window of the analyzed time segment, thus enabling the efficient extraction of temporal features without significant computational overhead. ... the model can learn the amplitude scaling and phase shift as a multiplication of complex numbers during the interpolation process.

mechanism: ATFNet measures periodicity by energy fraction of the dominant harmonic series (naive max-amplitude fundamental + harmonics) over total spectrum energy; that fraction becomes the adaptive weight for the frequency F-Block vs time T-Block ensemble. Extended DFT aligns lookback spectrum length to L+T full series basis.
data_needed: Per-channel DFT/Extended DFT spectrum; MainFreqWeight kernel; T-Block and F-Block forecast tensors
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Method/theory part; EURUSD H1 evaluation in Part 93
why_new_for_mis: Provides an explicit numeric periodicity/regime sensor (dominant-harmonic energy ratio) that can gate time vs frequency sensing paths in MIS.
quote: the degree of energy concentration within the dominant harmonic series in the frequency spectrum can reflect the periodicity of the time series. The ratio of the energy of the dominant harmonic series to the total energy of the spectrum can serve as a metric for quantitatively assessing the concentration of energy.

mechanism: CNeuronATFNetOCL runs T-Block (RevIN→transpose→PE→Patching→attention→projection→RevIN denorm) in parallel with F-Block (Extended FFT→complex RevIN→CNeuronComplexMLMHAttention→iFFT→reconstruct+forecast); WeightedSum blends forecasts using MainFreqWeights from dominant-harmonic energy; FreDF (p=0.8) reconciles multi-step spectrum.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr; patch config; complex attention heads/layers; NForecast; FreDF layer
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; OOS test with 31 trades (~61% wins reported)
why_new_for_mis: End-to-end dual-domain market sensor: local patch dynamics and global cyclic spectrum are fused with a data-dependent periodicity weight—MIS can log T/F branch disagreement as change/uncertainty.
quote: ATFNet applies dominant harmonic series energy weighting, extended Fourier transform, and complex spectrum attention to adapt to periodicity and frequency offsets in the input time series.

idea_name: S3 learned segment shuffle as input-organization sensor
mechanism: S3 Segment–Shuffle–Stitch splits HistoryBars into non-overlapping segments (e.g. 12 bars×BarDescr), learns SoftMax segment priorities P from a fixed-ones input via conv filters, differentiably permutes segments, then stitch-and-blend with learnable w1/w2 against the original series. Three stacked S3 layers (growing segment count) sit at Encoder input; shuffle params freeze after early training.
data_needed: HistoryBars=120, BarDescr=9; segment window 12*BarDescr; stacked ϕ S3 layers; NForecast=24
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test period shows Mon/Fri weakness, Wed strength
why_new_for_mis: Learns which historical segment order best exposes dependencies—MIS can treat converged shuffle indices and w_shuffled/w_original as a sensor of which past windows currently matter for the regime.
quote: S3 works by segmenting a time series into multiple non-overlapping segments, shuffling these segments into the most optimal order, and then combining the shuffled segments into a new sequence. It should be noted here that the order of segment shuffling is learned for each specific task.

idea_name: Per-indicator embedding channels for continuous weather-style dynamics
mechanism: Encoder splits each bar into five embedding windows {4,1,1,1,2} for candle body, RSI, CCI, ATR, MACD±signal so Continuous Attention and NeuralODE track each sensor channel’s continuous evolution separately—ATR/MACD become explicit volatility/momentum continuous trajectories.
data_needed: Per-bar state: close-open, high-open, low-open, tick_volume/1000, rsi, cci, atr, macd, sign
why_new_for_mis: Structures MIS inputs so volatility (ATR) and momentum (MACD) are first-class continuous channels under Continuous Attention, not mixed bar tokens.
quote: In my implementation, I split the source data as follows: 1. Description of the last candlestick (4 elements) 2. RSI (1 element) 3. CCI (1 element) 4. ATR (1 element) 5. MACD (2 elements)

idea_name: Historical masking degradation as temporal-dependence probe
mechanism: Client authors randomly replace up to 80% of historical values with 0; models whose forecast barely degrades are judged insensitive to temporal patterns. Used to motivate dropping intertemporal attention in favor of cross-variable attention plus linear trends for noisy FX.
data_needed: Multivariate lookback tensors with controllable zero-mask ratio; forecast error vs mask scale curves
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Paper experiment on multivariate LTSF; applied in EURUSD H1 Client implementation
why_new_for_mis: Offers a diagnostic sensing test: mask-sensitivity of any MIS encoder quantifies whether it truly reads temporal structure or only cross-sectional variable correlations.
quote: Models that are more sensitive to time dependence show a large performance degradation without correct historical data. ... Some such models show virtually unchanged forecasting performance even when up to 80% of historical data is randomly replaced with "0".

idea_name: Weekday profitability skew after S3 encoding
mechanism: After S3-augmented Encoder+Actor training on EURUSD H1, OOS report shows most losses on Mondays and Fridays and maximum profit on Wednesdays—suggesting calendar-day conditional policy behavior once segment shuffle exposes weekly structure.
data_needed: Per-weekday trade PnL from Strategy Tester; S3-shuffled 120-bar H1 windows
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; 2023 train; post-train test window
why_new_for_mis: Documents a concrete calendar-regime sensing outcome: MIS can gate or reweight policies by weekday when segment-level sensors reveal weekly inhomogeneity.
quote: If you look more closely at the testing report, you can highlight the most unprofitable Mondays and Fridays. On Wednesday, on the contrary, the model generates maximum profit.
